question: Is lv-icon's invented-number offload-invariant (WIN's read) or genuinely run-context-variant?

fixedConditions.note: ALL observations below at the auto 70% GPU load (no num_gpu forcing) unless noted; so any variance is NOT offload-fraction driven

observations.context: tool run 1 (mixed: visibletextmarker, mousedown, THEN lv-icon; lv 3rd in one load)
tool run 2 (isolated lv-icon sweep, auto phases first in a fresh load)
observations.note: CLEAN -- same 70% offload, different load context

observations.context: SEQ A controlled (lv-icon FIRST in a fresh load, x3)
SEQ B controlled (fresh load, visibletextmarker + mousedown FIRST, THEN lv-icon x3)
observations.note: FLIPS WITHIN ONE LOAD: rep1 invents, rep2/rep3 clean and byte-identical -> settles after the first call

finding: lv-icon's invented-number is RUN-CONTEXT NONDETERMINISTIC at fixed 70% offload / temp0 / seed0. Across loads it was observed BOTH [4,14,18] and clean, and within a single load (SEQ B) it flipped from [4,14,18] on the first call to clean on the next two. Output lengths differ (302 vs 346 vs 359) so this is CONTENT-level variance, NOT a scorer reading differently-worded-but-same output.
contrast: visibletextmarker's invented [5] is the opposite: byte-stable (len 380 every run) and offload-invariant (0% / 43% / 70% all invent 5). It is a ROBUST model-content hazard; lv-icon is an UNSTABLE borderline whose invented content depends on the model load history.
reconcileWithWin: WIN's read was right that this is a run-context (load-history) effect and NOT offload-fraction driven (all these are 70%); but the flip is at the CONTENT level (the numbers 4/14/18 are literally present or absent, lengths differ), not the scorer merely rescoring the same wording. It corrects my earlier 'lv-icon invents deterministically' note.
verdictImpact: qwen-as-GENERATOR drop STANDS and is REINFORCED: qwen is unreliable both as a stable inventor (visibletextmarker) and as an unstable run-context flipper (lv-icon). keep-as-JUDGE unaffected. vichange-conclusion-2381 verdict unchanged.
